items.claim: The unit's terminal boundary warrant leans on a verse whose ketiv/qere note it nowhere discloses, and two of its three full-verse Hebrew splices are paired with renderings that cover only part of the spliced run.
items.evidence: What verifies first: both cosmic onsets sit verse-initially in the pointed bytes, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה at oshb:Jer.31.35 and כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה at oshb:Jer.31.37 (byte tier, re-collated), and every parashah and seg disclosure matches the mark inventory exactly - setumah at MT 31:34, MT 31:36 and MT 31:37, paseq at MT 31:35 and MT 31:37 (single-witness WLC; tier-3 weak in the Prophets; paseq count-only, no position asserted). The seam itself is not contested. Defect one: the unit terminates itself on the incipit at web:Jer.31.38 and puts oshb:Jer.31.38 into its boundary evidence, but MT 31:38 carries a ketiv/qere note and no disclosure appears in any field. This is not a cosmetic omission here: a bare-consonant scan of the staged pointed text returns no unpointed token at all in MT 31:38, while returning קוה at MT 31:39 and השרמות at MT 31:40 - so the note has no visible locus in the running text, and a reader cannot check that the quoted opening clause falls clear of it. Where a ketiv/qere verse is put into evidence, the note is owed. Defect two: gloss extent does not match splice extent at two of the three sites. At oshb:Jer.31.36 the splice runs the whole verse through כָּל הַיָּמִֽים, but the paired rendering stops at the protasis, leaving the apodosis גַּם֩ זֶ֨רַע יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל יִשְׁבְּת֗וּ מִֽהְי֥וֹת גּ֛וֹי לְפָנַ֖י כָּל הַיָּמִֽים (oshb:Jer.31.36, byte) unglossed - although the if-then oath shape is the unit's own argument. At oshb:Jer.31.37 the splice again runs the whole verse while the rendering drops both the head messenger formula and the closing נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (byte). The evidence is therefore weaker than it reads: the reader is shown a formula-to-formula match that the paired renderings do not actually carry.

items.claim: The opening incipit, all three ketiv/qere sites, the parashah and paseq disclosures, and the note-count digit all verify against the pointed bytes and the mark inventory, including the byte-true observation that the opening verse's note has no visible unpointed alternate.
items.evidence: The incipit הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים stands verse-initially in MT 31:38 (byte tier, re-collated), so the fresh-topic onset is byte-anchored rather than asserted. Both visible ketiv/qere pairs stand in the bytes exactly as cited: ketiv קוה against qere קָ֤ו at oshb:Jer.31.39, and ketiv השרמות against qere הַשְּׁדֵמוֹת֩ at oshb:Jer.31.40 (byte). The careful statement that the note at the opening verse leaves no separately visible unpointed alternate is confirmed independently: a bare-consonant token scan of the staged pointed text returns nothing in MT 31:38 while returning the two ketiv forms just quoted at MT 31:39 and MT 31:40 - so the note is genuinely inventory-visible only, and the unit says so instead of inventing a locus. The note-count digit is exact: the inventory records four notes over four verses across MT 30:1 through MT 31:40 (MT 31:21, MT 31:38, MT 31:39, MT 31:40), three of which fall inside this span (sweep: 4 note-verses in range, 3 in span). Setumah at MT 31:37 and MT 31:40 and paseq at MT 31:40 match the inventory, and no further mark or note falls inside the span, so the disclosure set is complete rather than selective. The internal-split rejection is byte-consistent: no koh-amar, vocative or discourse imperative stands at any of the interior place-name turns in MT 31:39-31:40.

items.claim: The dated header's frame shape, both ketiv/qere sites, the royal name form, and the closing petuchah verify at byte tier against the frame and mark inventories, and the embedded messenger formula is attributed to a mouth rather than merely counted.
items.evidence: MT 32:1 opens verse-initially הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֤ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ (byte tier, re-collated) - the aleph-lamed form, and the site is a member of the eleven-verse prose-sermon superscription shape in the byte-swept frame inventory, not the one-site ayin-lamed variant that heads a different davar site in this book. The frame reading is therefore verified from the bytes and confirmed against the inventory rather than inferred from the formula's look. The date is header-internal, matching the class the date inventory records for this site, so the header is not miscast as a verse-initial date frame. Both notes stand in the bytes as cited: ketiv בשנת against qere בַּשָּׁנָה֙ at oshb:Jer.32.1 and ketiv עינו against qere עֵינָ֥יו at oshb:Jer.32.4 (byte); these are the only two notes the inventory records inside MT 32:1-32:5, so the disclosure set is complete. The royal name לִנְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּֽר at oshb:Jer.32.1 is the resh-family form, and the same base recurs as נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר at oshb:Jer.32.28 (byte) - both inventory members of that name form, with no blending into the nun-family spellings or the single plene byform elsewhere in the book. Petuchah at MT 32:5 and setumah at MT 31:40 match the inventory (single-witness WLC, tier-3 weak). The messenger formula inside MT 32:3 is handled correctly for this book's hardest formula hazard: it is named as the prophet's oracle quoted inside the king's question inside the narrator's report, so the formula is owned rather than counted.

items.claim: A digit-bearing naming claim about the scribe is contradicted by the bytes, the opening splice is described as a voice its own first words do not carry and is glossed by two words of a seven-word run, and the confidence sits above what the seam's signals support.
items.evidence: Defect one: the unit states the scribe is named three times across its span and reaches the third "by implication" at verse 14. The bytes carry the token in exactly two verses of MT 32:6-32:15, once each: בָּר֣וּךְ at oshb:Jer.32.12 and בָּר֔וּךְ at oshb:Jer.32.13 (byte tier, re-collated). MT 32:14 carries no such token, and the chapter's third site stands at MT 32:16 - outside this span. In a book where the same consonantal token also reads as a passive participle at two sites, a count reached by implication blends a naming with an inference, and the attested spelling is never named although the claim is explicitly about the spelling the bytes carry. Defect two: the opening splice runs the whole of MT 32:6, וַיֹּ֖אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ הָיָ֥ה דְּבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (byte), and is paired with a two-word rendering; the word-event clause that carries the seam's substance is left unglossed, and the splice's own first two words are third-person narration, not the first-person voice the sentence says they mark. Calibration: the onset at MT 32:6 is a member of none of the three word-event objects in the byte-swept frame inventory - the twenty-one-verse vayehi list, the eleven-verse hadavar list and the four-verse asher-hayah list all exclude it - so the seam rests on a person shift plus a first-person davar clause standing outside every inventoried frame object. That is a defensible seam, but it is the thinnest tier-1 warrant in the span and does not carry the highest confidence in this cluster. What verifies: the divine stack at oshb:Jer.32.14 and oshb:Jer.32.15 is the thirty-two-verse full-title signature object, correctly kept distinct from the bare tsevaot title; the paragraph fold inside web:Jer.32.8 is real and correctly held as formatting rather than evidence; petuchah at MT 32:5 and MT 32:15 and setumah at MT 32:14 match the mark inventory.

items.claim: The prayer's two divine-title invocations are point-correct members of the divine-title set, its note and seg disclosures match the inventory with nothing inside the span omitted, and the cross-seam echo is disclosed as texture rather than used as a warrant.
items.evidence: The invocation אֲהָהּ֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ at oshb:Jer.32.17 and its echo אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה at oshb:Jer.32.25 both stand in the bytes as cited (byte tier, re-collated), and both sites are members of the eleven qamats-pointed divine-title sites in the divine-name inventory - neither is one of the two hiriq-pointed courtly sites that stand elsewhere in this book's narrative zone. The point-aware split is therefore respected, not assumed. The unit also keeps its objects apart where it would have been easy to blend them: the tsevaot title standing inside the span at MT 32:18 is not folded into the thirty-two-verse full-title object, and no stack is claimed that is not quoted. The note stands in the bytes as cited: ketiv ובתרותך against qere וּבְתוֹרָתְךָ֣ at oshb:Jer.32.23 (byte), and it is the only note the inventory records inside MT 32:16-32:25. Paseq at MT 32:17 matches the inventory with no intra-verse position claimed, and the inventory records no petuchah or setumah anywhere inside the span - consistent with the unit asserting none, and absence is not treated as counterevidence. The verbal echo between MT 32:17 and MT 32:27 straddles this unit's own closing seam and is disclosed as cohesion rather than argued as a boundary signal, which is the discipline that seam requires. One minor observation, not a defect in the bytes: the category deviation for a prayer standing outside the book's named confession sites is disclosed in the rival-disclosure field rather than the device field.

items.claim: The closing warrant sentence attributes the high places to Molech, contradicting the construct chain it splices and the rendering it pairs with that splice, and the same field slices a ketiv/qere verse with no note disclosed in it.
items.evidence: Defect one: the prose calls the site the high places built for Molech, while the splice it introduces reads בָּמ֨וֹת הַבַּ֜עַל at oshb:Jer.32.35 (byte tier, re-collated) - the high places of Baal - and לַמֹּלֶךְ֒ stands ten tokens later in the same verse as the recipient of the child-transfer, outside the splice entirely. The rendering the unit itself supplies says the same thing: “They built the high places of Baal, which are in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to cause their sons and their daughters to pass through fire to Molech” (web:Jer.32.35). The sentence therefore misstates the run it is introducing, in the very clause that carries the unit's closing warrant; read back against its own splice and its own gloss, it does not survive. Defect two: that same field slices MT 32:35, a ketiv/qere verse (ketiv החטי against qere הַחֲטִ֥יא, byte), with no note disclosed in the field where the slice is taken; the disclosure appears only in the device field. The slice does in fact fall clear of the note - it is verse-initial while the pair is verse-final - so no counting hazard materialised, but in a book whose note inventory is this dense the disclosure belongs where the slicing happens. The inventory also records a paseq at MT 32:35, which this unit does not name although it owns that verse. What verifies: MT 32:26 opens verse-initially וַיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר (byte) and is a member of the twenty-one-verse vayehi word-event object in the byte-swept frame inventory, twenty of whose sites are verse-initial, so the onset claim is inventory-confirmed rather than assumed; נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר at oshb:Jer.32.28 is the same resh-family name form read at MT 32:1; the turn splice וְעַתָּ֕ה לָכֵ֛ן at oshb:Jer.32.36 is exact; the setumah at MT 32:35 matches the inventory. The seam itself is not contested.

items.claim: An exclusivity sentence enumerates three recurrence sites under a single byte label when only two of them are byte-identical, and the closing warrant sentence attributes the bound to the chapter division.
items.evidence: The construction sweep is right at the object level: the consonantal run of the quoted-objection phrase occurs in exactly three verses in the book (sweep: 3 verses - MT 32:36, MT 32:43, MT 33:10), so the exclusivity holds for the construction and the digit is sound. The tier does not. The sentence labels the quoted form byte at oshb:Jer.32.36 and then calls MT 32:43 and MT 33:10 recurrences without naming a tier for either. A byte sweep of that exact pointed run, אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֗ים, returns two verses (sweep: 2 verses - MT 32:36 and MT 32:43). At oshb:Jer.33.10 the run reads אֲשֶׁר֙ אַתֶּ֣ם אֹֽמְרִ֔ים, which differs in accentuation and carries an additional meteg: it fails byte, and it also fails accent-stripped, since that tier retains meteg - it matches only at the consonantal skeleton. A three-site recurrence claim carrying one tier label mixes tiers silently, and an exclusivity sentence is exactly where a tier label may not stand in for the sweep. Second: the closing sentence says the unit is bounded at the chapter division just before the next word-event. A chapter division is metadata that is never boundary evidence in either direction. The tier-1 word-event is named in the same sentence, so the substantive warrant is present, but the bound is attributed to the wrong object. What verifies, and verifies well: the other sweep is exact - אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת שְׁבוּתָ֖ם at oshb:Jer.32.44 (byte) is byte-identical in exactly two verses in the book (sweep: 2 verses - MT 32:44 and MT 33:26), correctly excluding the construct forms at MT 33:11 and MT 49:6 that a looser needle would have swept in. Setumah at MT 32:35 and MT 32:41, petuchah at MT 32:44, and paseq at MT 32:35, MT 32:36, MT 32:43 and MT 32:44 all match the mark inventory with nothing in the span omitted; the divine title at oshb:Jer.32.36 is the God-of-Israel form without tsevaot, kept distinct from the thirty-two-verse full-title object.

items.claim: The second word-event and its setting clause, the threefold self-naming, the causal binding at verse 4, and every mark and note inside the span verify against the pointed bytes and the inventories, with the divine-title objects kept apart.
items.evidence: MT 33:1 opens verse-initially וַיְהִ֧י דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ שֵׁנִ֑ית (byte tier, re-collated), and the site is a member of the twenty-one-verse vayehi word-event object in the byte-swept frame inventory - the membership is confirmed rather than assumed from the formula's look, which matters because the appended ordinal makes this shape look irregular. The setting clause וְהוּא֙ עוֹדֶ֣נּוּ עָצ֔וּר בַּחֲצַ֥ר הַמַּטָּרָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.33.1, byte) stands in the same verse, so the continuity with the preceding confinement setting is byte-anchored. MT 33:2 carries the divine name three times, as claimed. The formula at MT 33:4 is the God-of-Israel form without tsevaot - a distinct object from the thirty-two-verse full-title stack quoted earlier in the chapter before it - and it does open with the causal particle in the bytes, so the binding argued back to the invitation at MT 33:3 is byte-true rather than rhetorical. The note stands in the bytes as cited: ketiv לכול against qere לְכָל at oshb:Jer.33.8 (byte), and it is the only note the inventory records inside MT 33:1-33:9. Setumah at MT 33:3 and MT 33:9 and petuchah at MT 32:44 match the inventory, and the inventory records no paseq anywhere inside the span - consistent with the unit claiming none. Two minor observations, neither a defect in the bytes: the note at MT 33:8 rides on the quantifier rather than on the guilt noun the gloss names, and the splice at oshb:Jer.33.4 stops on a bare preposition while its paired rendering runs past it.
